name: warp_issue
kind: survey: cells, readings and how the readings decide between named alternatives; installs nothing
mechanisms: instruction issue (same-warp interval of a fixed-latency unit, yield bit, scheduler choice)
memory.constant_cache (h100 uniform first touch by warps per SM)
why: Questions left open by version 1 and by the re-reading of its data (dev/design/mechanism-recalibration.md section 6); each blocks a rule of issue_rules / constant_paths / kernel_boundary or the next install.
data_seen_before_freezing: warp_issue v1 with addenda; mechanism-recalibration.md section 6 (per-warp clock windows of d.add.s1, d.nop.s1.y1.w32, d.nop.s4.y1.w32; per-execution start levels; per-group clocks).

probe.chain: as version 1 (tools/microbench/ptx_kernel, gen.py plans, SASS gate = the plan). New in the generator: (1) a head clock: cells with suffix .hc read SR_CLOCKLO into a register of their own as the second instruction (after the stack load) and store it in the thread's fourth output word; (2) body forms `VIADD R4, R5, 0x1` (independent of its neighbours) next to the in-place `VIADD R5, R5, 0x1`; (3) shapes with 2, 3, 4 and 16 warps per CTA.

cells.e (same-warp interval): d.add.s{1,2,4} at .w4 (one warp per SMSP) and .w1 (one warp per SM). e.addx.s1 = 64 x `VIADD R4, R5, 0x1` (no add reads what a neighbour writes); e.addalt.s1 = 32 x [`VIADD R5, R5, 0x1`; `VIADD R4, R4, 0x1`]; both at the base shape and .w4. Expected values: d.add as version 1; e.addx leaves R5 unchanged; e.addalt reports the R5 count.
cells.e (scheduler): d.nop.s{1,2,3,4,8}.y1 with a head clock at 32 warps per CTA (.w32.hc) and d.nop.s4.y1 at 16 warps per CTA (.w16.hc): per warp three clocks (first instruction, body start, body end).
cells.g (start): h.empty.hc = stack load, head clock, prologue, clocks, stores, EXIT at the base shape, .w1, .w32, .g4, .g16. ncu per-SM instance values (--print-metric-instances values) of sm__cycles_active, sm__warps_launched and the stall ratios for a.empty, a.exit_only, b.sled.l8, d.nop.s8.y1 and h.empty.hc (kept as ncu_instances.csv next to ncu_metrics.csv; a reference-runner option).

runner: as version 1 (run.sh: direct value check, capture, two sampling passes with the metric list, replay with the engine build recorded in the run directory). Output $CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/stall-attribution/warp_issue-v2/<device>. Version 1 cells are not re-run.

derivation.per warp: clock windows per warp (analysis/warp_windows.py form): body length, start and end relative to the CTA's first warp, by SMSP (warp k on SMSP k mod 4, an assumption stated with the result).
derivation.usable: sampling readings from rows with at least 2000 samples in both passes; clock and counter readings from every row.

questions_before_data.same-warp interval: Per-warp body length of d.add.s1 at .w4: A1 = 2.0 cycles per add within 0.1 (the interval belongs to one warp's chain), A2 = 1.0. e.addx.s1: X1 = 2.0 per add (throughput of the unit for this form: any two consecutive adds of a warp are 2 cycles apart), X2 = 1.0 (the 2 cycles of the in-place chain belong to reading the register the previous add writes). e.addalt.s1: reported (1.0, 1.5 or 2.0 per add) with its math_pipe_throttle samples. At stall 2 and 4: time per add = max(stall, the stall-1 value) or reported.
questions_before_data.yield bit: d.nop.s1.y0 at one warp per SMSP: Y1 = 2.0 cycles per NOP (the warp itself skips a cycle), Y2 = 1.0 (it only gives way to another warp). d.nop.s0.y0.w4: reported against 33.4.
questions_before_data.scheduler: For each stall s the number of warps of an SMSP whose body windows overlap, their lengths, and the order of body starts and of first instructions by warp index; the description is reported, with the named candidates checked against it: round robin (all 8 share, 8 x 64 x s / min(8, s) each), youngest first by index (the s highest indices take 64 x s cycles each, the rest follow), least recently issued first.
questions_before_data.constants: h100 uniform first touch per load at 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 / 8 / 16 / 32 warps per SM: where the step from about 60 to about 130 lies and whether 3 warps give an intermediate value (3 warps = SMSPs 0-2). Vector path and b300: reported (expected flat).
questions_before_data.start: Per-SM sm__cycles_active of the empty kernels: G1 = the values form groups of about 16 (h100) / 18 (b300) SMs with a regular step inside a group (the first line reaches the SMs of a group one after the other); G2 = one common value per group with steps between groups; otherwise the distribution is reported. Head clocks inside a clock group: spread of the first instruction across SMs, and for .g4 / .g16 the first instruction of later CTAs against the last clock of earlier ones.

install: Nothing is installed from this version.
not_allowed: No value from another machine or from the literature; no full-GPU case.

addenda.when: 2026-11-16, h100 and b300 runs (37 new cells each, two sampling passes, replay with engine build 1a08913a; data $CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/stall-attribution/warp_issue-v2/{h100,b300}, tables derive-<device>.txt, per-warp windows windows-<device>.txt) — readings; nothing installed
addenda.text: All 37 cells built on both devices (0 unrealised), 37 / 37 captured, sampled twice and replayed. Value checks: wrong only where declared (d.add at stall 1 / 2) and in h.empty.hc, whose cells.tsv rows carry no expected value (generator gap; the clocks are used, not the value). e.addalt.s1 has RIGHT values on both devices (the prediction `hardware will lose adds` was wrong: the two chains are each 4 cycles apart, see below). SAME-WARP INTERVAL: A1 and X1 on both devices. One warp per SMSP or per SM runs 64 in-place VIADD in 129 cycles (2.02 per add, math_pipe_throttle 0.98 per add); 64 independent `VIADD R4, R5, 0x1` take the same 129 cycles; the alternating two chains too. With two warps per SMSP the holder takes 129 and the other warp waits for it and then takes 128 (independent adds as well). So two consecutive VIADD of an SMSP are 2 cycles apart whatever their registers, the idle cycle is not given to the other warp's VIADD, and the result latency (4) is covered by e.addalt's spacing. At stall 2 the time per add is 2.03, at stall 4 4.03 (= max(stall, 2)). Against the installed service leaf: VIADD has single_source_issue_interval 1.0 from alu_forms r2, which measured VIADD alternating with LOP3 at 1.0 cycle per instruction; both readings hold if the interval belongs to the instruction kind (adder against logic), not to the number of register sources. Not decided here: needs LOP3 after LOP3 and VIADD alternating with IADD3 (next survey, execution units). YIELD BIT: Y1 on both devices: at one warp per SMSP and at one warp per SM a NOP with yield bit 0 and stall 1 takes 2.03 cycles (class misc 0.99): the warp itself skips a cycle. Stall 0 with yield bit 0 at one warp per SMSP: 33.41 per NOP (wait 32.4), as at two warps. SCHEDULER (8 warps per SMSP, 64 NOPs, head clocks): stall 1: each warp runs its 64 NOPs alone in 66 cycles, one after the other. Stall 2 / 3 / 4: a group of 4 to 7 warps shares the slot evenly (each 64 x group size cycles: h100 stall 2 six warps 368-403, stall 3 seven warps 425-473, stall 4 seven 417-469 or five 372-378), the remaining 1 to 4 warps reach the body only when the group has finished and then share among themselves (130 / 195 / 260 = alone). Stall 8: all eight share (519-534). 4 warps per SMSP at stall 4: all share (260). The late warps are mostly the lowest-numbered ones, and their head clocks are the EARLIEST of the SMSP (they issue their first instruction first and are overtaken in the prologue). None of the three named candidates describes this: round robin would admit the late warps, youngest-first by index would let 2 (stall 2) or 4 (stall 4) warps finish in 128 / 256 cycles, least-recently-issued would admit the late warps at once. The rule stays open; what holds the early warps in the prologue (v1: not_selected on the last prologue instruction) needs per-pc sampling split by warp, which ncu does not give, or clocks between prologue instructions. CONSTANTS: h100 uniform first touch per load (at the load, imc_miss) by warps per SM 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 / 8 / 16: 60 / 65 / 95 / 127 / 129 / 122: no step but 31.5 cycles x max(2, number of SMSPs that hold a warp) (30.1 / 32.3 / 31.7 / 31.8 / 32.3 / 30.6 per unit). The installed few-warps pair (60.25 up to 2 warps, 129 above) is right at 1, 2, 4+ warps and 36 % high at 3 (replay 129 against 95). Vector path on h100 (90-97 at every shape) and both paths on b300 (uniform 63-72, vector 92-103) are flat. START: ncu's --print-metric-instances values changed nothing in the raw csv page on either version (same four aggregate columns): no per-SM values this way. Head clocks (first instruction of each SM's CTA, launch 0): 8 clock groups on both devices (h100 6 x 16 + 2 x 18 SMs, b300 16-20 SMs each): the groups are the GPCs. Inside a group the first instruction is issued over 39-60 cycles (h100, median 45; pairs of SMs a few cycles apart) / 27-45 (b300, median 32.5; regular: two SMs one cycle apart, the next pair 3-4 cycles later). So the first line reaches the SMs of a GPC within about 45 / 33 cycles, far less than the spread of sm__cycles_active between SMs (max - min about 160 on h100, 380 on b300). Reading (inference, G1 in kind but small): the first line arrives at nearly one time for the whole GPU, counted from the launch and not from each SM's entry, and the SMs become active one after the other (dispatch), so the SM that enters first waits longest and sets sm__cycles_active.max: entry step = (max - min) / CTAs = 1.2 cycles (h100, equal to the installed serial_ns_per_cta) / 2.6 (b300). kernel_boundary v1 gives every SM the mean wait after its own entry; a version 2 with a launch-level arrival and the entry stagger is the next install for this mechanism (it would put the empty kernel at about 465 / 880 against the hardware max 479 / 894).

addenda.when: 2026-11-16, correction to the START reading of the previous addendum (my inference, checked against version 1 data afterwards)
addenda.text: The inference `the first line arrives at one time for the whole GPU and the SM that enters first waits longest` does not hold on h100. Version 1 has the one-CTA shape a.empty.g1 (8 executions per device, counter sm__cycles_active.max = the single active SM): h100 319-367 (one execution 726), which is the MINIMUM of the all-SM shape (min 292-337, avg 364-411, max 446-490); b300 840-894, which is the MAXIMUM of the all-SM shape (min 483-566, avg 667-751, max 854-948). Under the entry-stagger reading a lone SM is the first to enter and should show the maximum: true on b300, false on h100. What the data allow: h100: a lone SM is served as fast as the fastest SM of a full launch, so the other SMs are slower because they are many (served one after another above the GPC: the head clocks show at most 45 cycles inside a GPC, the remaining 100+ cycles would be between GPCs, which the per-GPC clocks cannot show); b300: either the entry stagger, or a lone requester being slower than a crowd. Not decided on either device. The sentence about a kernel_boundary version 2 (`launch-level arrival and entry stagger`, 465 / 880) is withdrawn. Deciding cells for the next survey: a.empty with 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 33, 66 and all SMs occupied (grid as an absolute count): under an entry stagger the maximum stays and the minimum falls as SMs are added; under serial service the minimum stays and the maximum rises.
